category: F: quota, onboarding, profile and OAuth naming (MYEZ-012, 013, 018, 019, 025)
summary: All five Category F defects trace to code or config (origin/main 683f56c0). (012) The free credit is taken at the request gate before the products are identified. The only refund trigger is `result.success` being falsy (or an exception or disconnect). A partial result, an "Unknown Product" identity, an empty spec table or a result with no winner all come back as success:true, so they keep the debit and also bump the lifetime counter that the "N/3" pill reads. No existing flag covers this. The camera, URL and text routes all behave the same way (paid metering has been ON in prod since 2026-10-03). (013) Seven independent copy strings describe the quota with no server-provided rule or reset time. The "3/3 مجانًا" pill counts the lifetime-free counter, which never renews, while the banner promises daily and monthly renewal. CLAUDE.md:171 describes the rule as additive, but the code and the ToS count the first 3 inside the daily and monthly caps. (018) Production runs the 16-step authenticated sequence for 100% of users. Only priorities, budget and brand_attitude are required by a backend contract, and the PUT /demographics cohort seed can already set preferences_completed without them. Steps 1, 3, 5, 12, 13, 14 and 15 are purely presentational; attribution is a marketing question forced with no skip. Budget's title asks "Where do you usually shop?" but offers price tiers, and it collides with Step 4's "Where do you shop?". (019) The consent name comes from the Google Cloud project's OAuth consent-screen branding, which is outside the repo. The repo holds only the web and iOS client IDs. All 8 named client files contain "SmartCompare" only in a line-1 path comment, so none is user-visible. The fix is an owner action in the Google Cloud console with no binary change. (025) ProfileScreen.tsx:319-321 hard-codes `${governorate} · GCC` from the raw English enum, never reads the country, and falls back to "GCC" when the cohort match is weak. No country_code or governorate_code fields exist. Most fixes are client-side (1.0.1 or an OTA after approval). The backend parts are additive fields or one new dark flag (no-bill for unsupported results), each defaulting OFF.

defects.root_cause: consume_comparison_credit debits daily+monthly Redis credit atomically at the route gate BEFORE any identification or comparison (and on the lifetime-free path bumps daily/monthly too); the ONLY refund condition is a falsy `result.success` (or an exception / client disconnect). `success` means 'the pipeline returned a payload', not 'both identities resolved and a supported verdict exists': a hard-cap best-available PARTIAL, a one-sided Phase-1 failure (INSUFFICIENT_DATA requires BOTH sides to fail), a vision/URL placeholder identity ('Unknown Product'), an empty spec table or a no-winner result are all success:true, so they are treated as a delivery: credit kept, record_lifetime_comparison fires (the counter the pill reads), history row saved. The build-3 client independently decrements its pill on every success:true. There is no refund-on-low-quality path, no 'correct and recompare' credit, and no existing ENABLE_* flag for either.

defects.root_cause: There is no single source for the quota rule. /usage/status returns only counts, with no rule, no binding limit and no reset timestamp. The client renders the quota through seven independently written strings. The header pill counts the LIFETIME-free counter, which never renews (total = lifetime_free 3, used = users.lifetime_comparisons_used). The banner always says 'every day and at the start of each month', even when the monthly cap is the binding one. The Paywall says one of three other renewal sentences. Real rule (code): free = 3/day and 10/month (UTC calendar keys, so renewal is 03:00 Bahrain time). The first 3 'lifetime-free' comparisons bypass the caps but are still counted INTO the daily and monthly counters (not additive). The referral bonus adds to the monthly cap on a rolling expiry, not at month start. Premium: 10/day and 70/month.

defects.root_cause: App.tsx mounts NewOnboardingHost for every authenticated user with preferences_completed=false (CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT=100). The host hard-codes isAuthenticated=true, so the 16-step AUTHED_STEP_SEQUENCE runs [1 Welcome, 2 Language, 3 ValueProp, 4 Country(+BH governorate), 5 Trust, 6 Age, 7 Gender, 8 Priorities, 9 Budget, 10 BrandAttitude, 11 Attribution, 12 CohortProof, 13 Anticipation, 14 Loading (3.2 s floor), 15 Reveal, 17 Notifications], followed by the AI-consent sheet before the first compare. Client validation forces language, country, priorities, budget, brand_attitude AND attribution (no skip on 11). Only priorities, budget and brand_attitude are required by a backend contract (PUT /auth/preferences, which sets preferences_completed). Country and language are optional and server-derived. Country does not even change region or currency (the client hard-codes 'bahrain'). Age, gender and governorate are cohort demographics; attribution is marketing; steps 1, 3, 5, 12-15 make no network call. The budget step's title 'Where do you usually shop?' / 'أين تتسوق عادةً؟' offers price tiers and nearly duplicates Step 4's 'Where do you shop?' / 'من أين تتسوق؟'.

Drop or shorten 1/3/5/12/13/14/15 to a single intro plus reveal, make Attribution skippable (isStepValid case 11) or move it post-value, and defer Age/Gender/Governorate to the existing DemographicsBottomSheet after the first result. defects.root_cause: The 'continue to SmartCompare' text is the App name on the OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform -> Branding) of the Google Cloud project that owns BOTH OAuth clients the app uses. The web and iOS client IDs share one project-number prefix. They were created in Session 16 (Mar 2026), when the product was named SmartCompare. The app uses the native @react-native-google-signin SDK (iOS client) and sends the idToken to Supabase signInWithIdToken, so Google shows the project's branding, not Supabase's domain. Nothing in the repo sets that name: no google-services.json or GoogleService-Info.plist, no scopes beyond the defaults. In-app branding is already MYEZ (CFBundleDisplayName, app.json name). The 8 named client files contain 'SmartCompare' only in a line-1 file-path comment, so none is user-visible.

defects.root_cause: ProfileScreen builds the subtitle as `${cohortDisplay.governorate} · GCC` from /auth/cohort-profile. That field echoes the raw onboarding enum value (English code 'Northern'), and the string appends a hard-coded literal 'GCC'. It is not localized and never reads the country the user picked ('BH'). Country and governorate live only inside users.demographics_profile JSONB as country ('BH' from the client, 'Bahrain' or a raw ISO code when server-derived) and governorate ('Northern'). No country_code, governorate_code or display_label fields exist. The Arabic labels already exist in i18n (onboarding.s4.bahrain, onboarding.s4.gov_northern) and Step15Reveal uses them, but ProfileScreen and the Results CohortBadge do not.

extra_findings.evidence: HomeScreen.tsx:160-176 reads referral status monthly_bonus_comparisons, which is users.referral_bonus_comparisons_this_month (referral_service.py:540,567). usage_service.py:588-596 says that counter MUST NOT drive entitlement; /usage/status limits.monthly_bonus (usage_service.py:744-746) is the authoritative sum (measured).

extra_findings.title: W4-13b (#215): SSE stream bills success:False terminals
extra_findings.evidence: text_routes.py:1220-1297 meters STREAM_TIMEOUT / INSUFFICIENT_DATA / moderation terminals as a delivery (comment :1227); the orchestrator yields them as settle_complete/complete (structured_comparison_service.py:4777-4787, 5003-5037, 5518). Build 3 uses REST because ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE_DEFAULT=false (features.ts:52) (measured).

extra_findings.title: Slow-success edge: client gives up at 35 s while the server can still bill
extra_findings.evidence: COMPARE_TIMEOUT_MS=35000 (api.ts:48) vs STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS 30.0 in prod (CLAUDE.md:337), with the preferences fetch, the consume and the history write outside the cap. A success:true landing after the axios timeout is billed (text_routes.py:886-951) while the user saw the timeout alert. No disconnect detection exists on the REST route. Inferred.

extra_findings.title: Step 9 budget tiers mean different money per category
extra_findings.evidence: Onboarding shows fixed BHD bands <11 / 11-57 / 57-189 / 189-500 / 500+ (en.json:604-613), but scoring maps prices to tiers per category, e.g. fragrances 30/80/180/500 and electronics 100/400/800/2000 (scoring_service.py:555-559). The answer the user gives is interpreted against different thresholds (measured).

extra_findings.title: CLAUDE.md freemium rule contradicts code and ToS
extra_findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:171 says 'Free 3 lifetime + 10/mo + 3/day'. The code counts the lifetime-free 3 inside the daily and monthly counters (usage_service.py:314-327, 360-365), and ToS terms_of_service.md:25 states 'your first 3 comparisons count toward these limits' (measured).

extra_findings.title: Every re-compare after a correction costs a new credit
extra_findings.evidence: The gate consume (text_routes.py:833) runs before any cache lookup or compare (:846); no retry or recompare grant exists in app/. Audit 012 expects 'correct the products and recompare without a new debit' (measured).

extra_findings.title: Two near-identical onboarding questions with different meanings
extra_findings.evidence: Step 4 'من أين تتسوق؟' / 'Where do you shop?' (country; ar.json:546-549, en.json:549-552) vs Step 9 'أين تتسوق عادةً؟' / 'Where do you usually shop?' (price tier; ar.json:600, en.json:603) (measured).
